subject: Business Models
title: Yahoo: The Portal That Missed Everything
description: A quick, practical guide to Yahoo: The Portal That Missed Everything.

hook.text: Yahoo was valued at $125 billion in 2000. It sold to Verizon for $4.5 billion in 2017. A 96% value collapse.

buildup.text: Yahoo was the internet's homepage: email, news, sports, finance—all in one portal.

discovery.text: Yahoo could have bought Google for $1M in 1998, then again for $5B in 2002. It passed both times.

twist.text: Yahoo also rejected Facebook's acquisition offer and failed to acquire YouTube. It missed every major shift.

climax.text: Yahoo's portal model assumed users wanted a curated homepage. Google proved they wanted a search box.

punchline.text: $125B to $4.5B. Passed on Google, Facebook, YouTube. Three strikes, you're out.

quiz.question: Which company did Yahoo famously pass on buying twice?

details.summary: Yahoo was the internet's starting page, valued at 125 billion dollars in 2000. It passed on acquiring Google for 1 million dollars, then for 5 billion dollars, and failed to acquire Facebook. Despite enormous traffic, it never built a durable search engine, social network, or content platform.
details.whyItMatters: Yahoo had more internet traffic than any company in the 2000s but failed to convert it into a lasting competitive advantage. Its story shows that traffic and brand alone cannot sustain a technology company without a clear, defensible core product.
takeaways: Yahoo passed on acquiring Google for 1 million and later for 5 billion dollars
Despite massive traffic, no single product achieved lasting market dominance
Verizon acquired Yahoo's core business for 4.5 billion, a fraction of peak value

faq.question: Why did Yahoo decline despite being the most visited website?
faq.answer: Yahoo spread resources across dozens of products without achieving dominance in any category. Google dominated search. Facebook dominated social. YouTube dominated video. Yahoo was a jack-of-all-trades, master of none, with no defensible moat to protect its traffic.

faq.question: Could different strategic decisions have saved Yahoo?
faq.answer: Acquiring Google in 2002 for 5 billion would have given Yahoo search dominance. Buying Facebook in 2006 would have secured social. Either acquisition alone could have transformed the company. Yahoo's indecision and lowball offers cost it two generation-defining platforms.
